baseline.name: Simulate every reduction with a full-array maximum search
baseline.approach: For each legal operation, scan to find the current largest and next distinct largest, then change one occurrence.
baseline.time: O(n*T) for T reduction operations; O(n^3) upper bound when T=O(n^2)

archived.name: Sort once and accumulate distinct-value tiers
archived.time: O(n log n) with a qsort implementation providing that sorting bound, plus an O(n) scan; C does not mandate qsort's worst-case complexity
archived.space: qsort workspace is implementation-dependent; the explicit accumulation uses O(1) state

why: A value's rank among distinct levels directly counts how many reductions it needs, so the operations need not be performed one at a time.
quantitative_comparison: With all values distinct, T=n(n-1)/2 individual reductions. This archive does one sort and n-1 adjacent-level updates/accumulations after sorting. It skips explicit simulation of T reductions, but sort/library costs prevent a fixed runtime factor.
tradeoffs: Mutates input and relies on qsort's actual algorithm/workspace. The int total assumes bounded problem sizes.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
